entries.semantic_reason: Only splash candidate in the XD corpus, and the historically calibrated XD reference artboard. The XD source text reads "Bictov"; branding normalization to "Merzox" is the existing exporter's --normalize-merzox-brand behaviour and is never reimplemented in the comparator.

The Flutter onboarding initial state is the offers concept, and this XD state is "أفضل الخصومات" (offers and discounts). The other onboarding candidates are the map and payment states. Flutter wording and XD wording are NOT text-identical; this is a semantic state match, not text parity.

The Flutter seed renders businessMode=false, i.e. the customer flow, and this XD artboard is the customer login ("لمواصلة استخدام التطبيق"). The alternative artboard e1a55414-b8c0-4225-be71-3e7df543e421 is the merchant login and explicitly says "كتاجر".

The Flutter seed renders the untouched customer SignupPage in its Arabic idle state. This exact-name 375x812 XD artboard is the customer signup state and links directly to the locked customer login artboard. The suffixed artboards are separate signup variants. Its legacy logo stores a vector mark beside the exact text tail 'ictove'; the shared exporter normalizes that rendered tail to 'Merzox' without changing the XD package, node ids or node names.

This is the explicit "معاينة المتجر" merchant-preview artboard, containing the store sections خدماتنا, عن المتجر, المنتجات and التقييمات. The long "معاينة" alternatives encode shopper/product/review states with customer actions such as add-to-cart and review composition.

The Flutter seed renders the shell on tab 1 with isGuest=true, i.e. the UNAUTHENTICATED cart. This exact-name 375x812 artboard is that state: the guest avatar mark, the sign-in prompt, the two account actions and the shell bottom navigation with the cart entry active. The suffixed السلة artboards encode the authenticated basket states (populated and empty) and are separate seeds, not variants of this one.

The Flutter seed renders a placed order whose only reached step is "placed", which is the state this exact-name 375x812 artboard draws: the success headline, the order-number card and a four-step timeline with the first entry complete. The suffixed تتبع الطلب artboards encode the later steps and are separate seeds.

The only من نحن artboard in the corpus. The Flutter seed renders the server-driven page in its loaded state with all three sections collapsed, which is what the artboard draws. Its wordmark is the all-caps legacy form, normalized to MERZOX by the exporter without changing the XD package.

The Flutter seed renders the PRODUCTS tab of the favourites page, which is the tab this artboard shows selected. NOTE: the artboard puts a photograph in every card and the seed deliberately carries no image URL - a golden must not fetch one - so each card reaches its placeholder branch. The image regions therefore differ by construction and dominate this seed's metrics; they are not a layout mismatch.

The entry state of the 40-artboard تفاصيل المتجر family, and the only one at 375x810 - the rest are taller scroll states. It is the CUSTOMER view of the same page معاينة المتجر shows in merchant preview: it carries the notification bell, the chat affordance and the shell bottom navigation, which the preview artboard deliberately has none of. Seeding both modes keeps that difference measured rather than assumed. The logo card holds the artboard's sample store artwork against the seed's placeholder, for the same reason as every other image-bearing seed: a golden cannot fetch one.

The المنتجات tab of the storefront: the tab strip with the middle entry active, the الجديدة/الأكثر مبيعًا/عروض filter row and the product grid. Six artboards in the family draw this state; this is the first. Cropped to the first viewport - the artboard draws its below-the-fold grid inline. Product images are the artboard's photographs against the seed's placeholders, and the floating chat bubble is pinned to the viewport in the app while the artboard draws it at the document end.

The التقييمات tab: the composer - stars, comment field and publish button - above the published list. The composer is only rendered for a signed-in customer the backend has judged eligible, so the seed supplies both rather than capturing the sign-in gate, which is a different state from this artboard. Cropped to the first viewport.

The product page in its idle description state: the image carousel, the price and name, the الوصف tab selected, the quantity stepper, the shade variants and the seller block. Chosen over تفاصيل المتجر – 14, which draws the transient "added to cart" toast, and over the 1141-tall artboards, which are its التقييمات tab. Despite the family name these artboards are the PRODUCT page, not the storefront. Product photography is the artboard's against the seed's placeholder, as in every image-bearing seed.

Step one of checkout. The artboard offers a LIST of previously used addresses; a user document holds a single address string, so this step shows that one and offers to replace it. The address book is backend work, and drawing a list the system cannot populate would be a lie rather than a fidelity gain.

Step two at rest. Re-pointed from `تفاصيل المتجر – 24`, which is the same screen with the cancel button filled and a line explaining the twenty-four hour window — the state after the customer has reached for cancel, not the one the step opens in. Board 26 fills `تأكيد الطلب` and outlines `الغاء الطلب`; this screen had it the other way round, which put the weight of the page on the button that throws the order away.

The MERCHANT home. Of the twelve الرئيسية artboards only two are the customer home, and both carry an unsupported backdrop blur that the comparator refuses fail-closed, so they are not seeded. This one is clean and is the merchant shell dashboard: the sales/orders/visits figures and the recent-order table.

The merchant shell's orders tab. The artboard titles itself "الطلبات", searches by order number and customer name, filters by a single order status and tabulates every status at once — which is what the seed renders. Three further artboards (11, 12, 17) are states of this same screen and are not separately seeded.

The merchant shell's products tab. The artboard titles itself "المنتجات" and lists 127-tall cards carrying a photo, a name, price, quantity, classification and a published corner. The seed serves four products with no image URL, so the photo area is the local placeholder rather than the artboard's photograph: that difference is the bulk of this seed's residual and is not a layout defect. Three further artboards (13, 15, 16) are states of this same screen.

The customer home in its GUEST state: the header greets a visitor with a plain avatar and no name. Both home artboards were unmeasurable until the exporter learned to render backdrop blur: a single 98x35 frosted chip on the promotional card counted as an unsupported node, and the comparator is fail-closed. The 1716 height is the corpus convention for drawing what scrolling reveals, so only the top 812 - what a device shows - is measured. Two thirds of this seed's residual is photography, not layout: the artboard's promotional card is a dark sale photograph and its store cards carry a logo, while the catalogue API exposes no artwork for a business at all - only the deterministic placeholder colour the cards already use. The 112-row carousel band alone measures ~150 mean delta against a flat placeholder. The structural bands themselves land within a few pixels: carousel 113..223 exactly, dots and search within one, section heading and shelf within four. The bottom navigation is ~11 shorter on the artboard; it is shared with five other seeds, so it is left alone rather than re-baselining them for about a point of MAE.

The same screen SIGNED IN: the header carries the customer photo and name. It is the only difference between the two artboards, which is why they share one seed API and differ only in the session. Both home artboards were unmeasurable until the exporter learned to render backdrop blur: a single 98x35 frosted chip on the promotional card counted as an unsupported node, and the comparator is fail-closed. The 1716 height is the corpus convention for drawing what scrolling reveals, so only the top 812 - what a device shows - is measured. The 112-row carousel band alone measures ~150 mean delta against a flat placeholder. The structural bands themselves land within a few pixels: carousel 113..223 exactly, dots and search within one, section heading and shelf within four. The bottom navigation is ~11 shorter on the artboard; it is shared with five other seeds, so it is left alone rather than re-baselining them for about a point of MAE.

The conversation inbox with its all/unread tabs, on the "all" tab: four rows alternating read and unread, which is what this board draws. Three sibling boards (الرسائل – 3, and two more) are the same surface on the other tab or with a different row count. The seed renders the inbox view alone rather than inside the customer shell, because the merchant shell hosts the same widget and the artboard draws no chrome around it beyond the bottom navigation.
The inbox with nothing in it. The artboard draws a paper-plane illustration over an apology and a hint to go ask a store about a product; the app draws an icon over the same two lines.
The notifications list. It is drawn inside the الرسائل family but is a different surface: its own page, its own bloc, and rows that carry an event rather than a conversation.

The third and last checkout step. The artboard draws a courier, a success line, the order number and two ways on. The app declared this step in its enum and never rendered it: a successful checkout emptied the cart and the page popped itself away, so the customer got a snackbar where the design gives them their order number. The courier illustration is not in the asset bundle, so the icon standing in for it is the one the tracking screen already uses for a delivery in progress.
The search screen before a query: the field, the "previously searched" heading with its clear link, and the recent rows each with their own remove. One sibling board is the same surface.
Search results on the products tab. The artboard grids them three across; the app grids two, which is the bulk of this residual.
The same results on the stores tab. Both artboards draw a store logo the catalogue does not expose, so the tiles here carry the placeholder the rest of the app uses.

The customer profile menu, signed out: a greeting with no name over edit-profile, my-orders, map, favourites, about-us, a notification toggle and share. Its signed-in sibling `البروفايل – 2` differs only in the avatar and the name. The residual is one deliberate divergence: the artboard draws the whole menu for a signed-out visitor with a register button, and the app draws a sign-in gate instead. Every row below that header — my orders, favourites, edit profile — needs an account, so the gate asks once rather than letting five rows refuse in turn.

The merchant profile menu: the store logo and name over personal profile, store settings, messages, contact us, preview my store and an order-notification toggle. Rebuilt from a profile card to this menu, 40.08 -> 15.16. Two of its rows had no way in before: the merchant's own messages were reachable only from the dashboard header, and there was no contact route at all.
The profile form. `الملف الشخصي` draws the same surface with name, phone and email; this board adds gender and a birth date, which is the one the app implements.

Store settings in the state the screen opens in: the first section showing. Re-pointed from `4c608328`, which is the same screen with every section collapsed and is seeded separately as `store_settings_closed` — the app opens one section, so measuring it against the closed board was measuring the wrong state.

The customer’s order history on its first tab. `تفاصيل المتجر – 22` and `– 37` are the same tab; 22 is the one that keeps `تتبع الطلب` on the card, which is the only route a customer has to the tracking screen. Both boards draw the first card slid aside over an orange `الغاء الطلب` running off the far edge — a swipe caught mid-gesture, which the seed captures at rest.
The same screen on `المكتملة`, where the card keeps its total and drops the tracking chip. `– 36` is this board with `رقم الطلبية` for `رقم الطلب` and is otherwise identical.
The same screen on `الملغية`, whose card carries one extra line: why the order was cancelled. `– 21` is this board with the other spelling of the order-number label.

Order history with nothing in it. Drawn in the cart family but titled `طلباتي`, and it is the one board of the seven with no tab strip: a customer with no orders has no groups to move between. It is also the only one that draws the bottom bar, which the loaded boards omit.

The merchant’s product form as it opens: the quantity field showing and neither tick box set. 1334 tall with the shell’s own bar drawn across the fold, which is a full screen the form scrolls inside — the reason the editor stopped being a bottom sheet.

The same form with both boxes ticked. `غير محدودة` takes the quantity field away and `هناك تخفيض` puts the price the customer pays in its place, and the two cancel out: everything from `تصنيف المنتجات` down sits at the same height on both boards.

The options dialog over the form: name an option, press the plus, and it becomes a chip. The board sets the panel 298 down a 1251-tall artboard, its foot against the bar rather than its middle against the screen’s, so a centred dialog sits about a hundred pixels higher than the reference and that is most of this seed’s difference.

One order in the merchant’s hands, newly arrived. The board carries no page title — the screen is reached by tapping one row of a list that is already titled, and the order number is the first thing on it.

The status control open. The board lists four — قيد التجهيز, في الطريق, تم التسليم, ملغي — which is every status except the one a new order can actually move to next. The server enforces the lifecycle and would answer three of those four with a 409, so the menu offers what is permitted rather than what is drawn, and this seed shows two items where the reference shows four.

The order moved on and the customer told about it. `إرسال إشعار` is what the board puts beside the status control and what this pass added an endpoint for: it re-sends the status the server already believes, once a minute at most. The board floats its confirmation across the middle of the screen; a snackbar sits at the foot of it, which is most of this seed’s difference.
What `عرض الفاتورة` opens. A page with a printer at the head of it rather than the bottom sheet it used to be: this is a document, not a summary raised over the screen it came from.

The product page on its reviews tab, with the composer a signed-in eligible customer sees. `– 35` and `– 38` are the same surface and differ only in what the header carries — `– 38` a close button and a `جديد` ribbon over the photograph. The board puts the reviewer’s own avatar and name above the stars; nothing on this screen knows who is signed in, and the storefront composer this one now matches does not draw it either. Most of this seed’s difference is the photograph: the board carries a real product shot across the top 300 pixels and the repository ships none, so the capture falls back to its placeholder. Below the fold the two agree closely.

Step one on the branch where there is no saved address to pick. `– 16`, already seeded, is the other branch; these are two states of one step, not two versions of it, which is why the form now carries the wizard’s header and its three chips. `– 25` and `– 40` are this board with the `تمت إضافة العنوان بنجاح` bar over it. Two departures: the board puts a `+972` country prefix on the phone field, which needs a country list and a storage format the server does not have today; and `تفاصيل العنوان` is not on the board and is kept, because a governorate with a city is not an address a driver can find.

The governorate picker, raised over the step it belongs to. The list is the server’s own — `backend/src/policies/address.policy.js` — so the three the board tags `مغلق` are listed and disabled here too: a customer can see the place exists and is not served rather than wonder why it is missing.

The city picker, which only ever holds cities of the governorate above it — the board lists the towns of رام الله والبيرة, and so does this seed, because that is the governorate it was reached through.

Every registered shop, two to a row, under a search field of its own. Not a tall screen: 1492 is what scrolling reveals, and `المتاجر – 1` is this board with the bottom bar drawn across the fold, which is where it sits on a device. The board reserves a `مساحة إعلانية` banner after every four cards; nothing in this app or its server has ad inventory, and a slot with nothing in it is worse than no slot, so it is not built. The two round faces on each card are emoji, which the golden environment has no font for and a device does. Above the first card the two agree closely; the cards themselves differ mostly because the board carries each shop’s real wordmark and the capture falls back to a placeholder.
The same screen with the logo section open. Only one section is ever open, so the store name goes away as the logo arrives — which is what makes these four boards four surfaces rather than one.

The description section: the blurb, the address and what the shop sells. Two fields under it are not on the board — the English name and the registration attachment — and are kept, because enrollment collects both and this screen is now their only editor.
The four ways a customer can reach the shop outside the app.
Slide two: the map. As with the first slide, the Flutter wording and the XD wording are not text-identical — this is a semantic state match, not text parity.
Slide three: paying. The last slide drops the skip, because there is nothing left to skip.

A basket with something in it. The seeded `cart_guest` is `السلة`, which is the signed-out gate; these are three states of one tab. Reaching it needed the cart tab to stop building its own bloc on a real `ApiService` — nothing could put a line in the basket from a test.
The same tab, signed in, with nothing in it yet.
Favourites on the stores tab, which is the tab the bloc opens on; the seeded `favorites` is the products one.
The order being prepared: two steps reached, and the address still changeable.
The order on its way, with the driver named. The driver’s card appears only once there is one.

The delivered order with the review over it. It was at the foot of the page instead — below a four-step timeline and a driver’s card, which on an 812 screen is below the fold, where an invitation nobody sees is not an invitation. Dismissing the sheet leaves the same composer at the bottom, so it is an offer and not a toll.

Not the customer signup `إنشاء حساب` draws: both this board and `– 2` say `ابدأ في إنشاء حسابك بخطوتين` and the second asks for a shop, so they are the merchant enrolment wizard. Step one is who is signing up. The board puts a `+972` prefix on the phone field, which needs a country list and a storage format the server does not have today.
Step two: what they are opening. Reached the way a merchant reaches it, because the first step will not hand over an unfilled form.
The gate in front of the inbox, for a customer who has not signed in.
The inbox on its unread tab. The seeded `messages_inbox` is the same view on `الكل`; the second board of this surface is this one with a second row.

A conversation from the customer’s side. The board puts what you wrote at the START of the row in #3D5A80 and what you were told at the end in #F9F9F9 — the sides a reader of any direction expects, rather than mirroring with the language; this screen had it the other way round and in orange. The board draws no per-bubble timestamps and a paperclip and an emoji in the composer: the times are kept, because a conversation without them is worse, and there is no upload endpoint anywhere in this repository for the paperclip to reach.
The same six lines from the other end. `isMine` is what decides a bubble’s side, so the shop’s screen is the customer’s with that flag inverted.
The orders filter raised over the orders tab: order number, customer name, a date range and a status.
What a product card’s menu offers. A live product is offered hiding and never showing, and deleting asks first — `– 15`, the board this one clusters with, is that question.
The products filter: a name, a state and a classification.

The product’s images. Built with a documented departure that still stands: no upload endpoint, storage or multipart route exists anywhere in this repository, so the screen orders and names image URLs rather than accepting a file.
The same screen with every section collapsed, which is what tapping the open one gives back — the menu the four editors hang off.

A thread nobody has written in yet. The board opens it with a banner rather than a line of grey text: keep the conversation here, and here is who to tell if something goes wrong — which is a safety notice, not decoration, so it replaced the generic line. The board also draws a camera in the composer and an attached photo above it; no upload endpoint exists anywhere in this repository.
The same thread three lines in. The banner is gone by then, on the board and here: it belongs to a thread nobody has written in yet.

What `الغاء الطلب` asks before it throws the basket away — it used to ask nothing. The board asks twice: first whether to cancel, then for a reason under a second button. The reason half belongs to cancelling a PLACED order, and `طلباتي` already asks for one there; nothing has been placed at this point in the wizard, so there is nothing to record a reason against. Most of what is left after matching the scrim is that difference in size: a panel that asks one question is a good deal smaller than one that asks two and carries a text area between them.

The profile form with every placeholder still showing. `تعديل الملف الشخصي`, already seeded, is the same screen with an account behind it — the two boards are one form before and after it has been used, not two forms. The board puts a `+972` prefix on the phone field, which needs a country list and a storage format the server does not have today.

Step two after the customer has reached for cancel and said no: the button keeps the emphasis and the twenty-four hour window stays beside it. Three boards, three states — `– 26` at rest with no rule on it, this one, and `– 30` for the question. The window used to be printed under the buttons at all times, which put a rule about undoing an order on a screen where nothing had been ordered.
